newsitem.title: UK: NWE STRAIGHT-RUN FUEL EDGES LOWER, BUYERS AT BAY.
newsitem.headline: NWE STRAIGHT-RUN FUEL EDGES LOWER, BUYERS AT BAY.

text.p: Euro low sulphur straight-run edged a little lower on Tuesday with offers in the $111/$112 region but buyers continued to hold their cards close to their chests, traders said.
"We proposed above $110 without giving any specific number and we have buyers a little lower at $106/$107," one seller with an end month 25,000-tonne loader of low sulphur material said.
Three other cargoes were heard on offer, loading August 15-25, August 20-30 and August 31, with at least one of the sellers at $111.
"Prices are a little down as the market is too dull, there's been no serious buying interest for a week or more," a second seller said.
Up to four buyers were heard on the market but few were indicating solid bids. Little buying interest was seen from the United States.
"One major was at $106 and others are not showing their hands yet...If European prices stay around $107 we will sell trans-Atlantic," a trader with a refiner said.
An independent trader that was showing a cargo acquired recently at about $110/111 last week may be taking it to the United States, where it may have an outlet too use the cargo itself.
Traders said Russian high sulphur straight-run was static with refiners holding back before levels fell further in line with crude to make it an attractive purchase.
M-100 was heard offered steady to a little weaker at two means +$3/4 with buyers $1 to $2 lower while at least two E-4 cargoes were at about three means +$2.
